Deliverable: a short finding in rules/slow-commands.md with measured stage times, plus a ranked list of fixes with estimated savings (candidates, untested: merge adjacent boxes into larger fills, fewer and larger readback scans, avoid re-reading surface already probed). tasks.title: Share residential frontage surfaces, boundaries and access between ground and decor
tasks.notes:
Covers Suburban streets lack distinct frontages, boundaries and entrance connections (I-042), sparse Kitchener Road snag (S-073), southampton-build. Owner approved diagnosis, inference preference and this independently reviewed task on 2026-11-01.
Cause: ground.classify uses map/aerial colours and generic shade filling without garden plot or entrance intent; guessed lawn near any road/building can become paving. garden_sources already grows approximate plots and consumes street/per-property boundary conventions, but Kitchener's convention has selected hedge vetoes and no front fence/wall specification. Boundary generation reserves no entrance gaps or connections. The saved decor report consists of aerial hedges and mapped iron bars. Unverified: exact plots/gates and how many visible columns the paving conversion caused.
Deliver one shared residential frontage description consumed by the existing ground and decor passes: private frontage extent/surface, boundary segments, entrance opening and connection. Reuse existing plots/segments and convention files; no new pass or parallel geometry engine. Use lib/site/provenance.py and existing evidence IDs, retaining property/street scope and reason for inference through plans/reports. Replace the lossy garden tuple/provenance conversion and superseded access-blind joining path.
Evidence: explicit property observation > street-run evidence > labelled deterministic same-street inference. Owner prefers a coherent realistic street from best available evidence over leaving gaps because exact detail is uncertain. Inferred private frontages require identified residential properties and supporting frontage/street evidence; missing conventions alone do not authorize fences. Explicit open frontages, none vetoes and per-house overrides win. Do not randomize surfaces for variety. Retain observed gravel/paving/green differences and distinguish private frontage from public pavement; constrain generic guessed-lawn conversion accordingly. Nonresidential/campus behaviour must remain compatible.
Pass responsibility: feature owns the building/porch, threshold and feature-generated external landing/steps/supports, even outside the mapped footprint. Keep existing placement and journal ownership semantics. Expose a small shared read-only entrance-approach description: actual door, feature approach extent, usable outward connection point/height/direction, clearance and provenance; distinguish generated door positions from observed ones. Ground owns remaining frontage/pavement surfaces and onward route, joining the outer end of the feature approach (door when no approach), without duplicating or replacing feature steps. Decor owns boundary/furniture/gate placement and preserves the route/opening/headroom; it does not construct a second threshold, stair or path. Respect existing trees.
Solid feature steps/landings/supports retain journal ownership. Required clear space is shared semantic planning data, not ownership of air: preserve journal CANCEL/air-cancels rules. Ground/decor must not fill reserved clearance or replace feature solids. Reserve access across mapped, convention, designer and aerial candidates AND final join_pieces/straightening. Explain conflicts with explicit observed boundaries rather than silently erasing them. Preserve lidar heights, masks, ownership, clipping and undo. Blocked connections report endpoints, responsible pass and reason; do not bypass protected blocks or alter the house to force access.
Legacy approaches: use narrowly scoped read-only reconstruction from the landed plan/journal where trustworthy; otherwise label generated/inferred data and unavailable endpoints. A plausible inferred entrance may guide the frontage but cannot be reported as a verified connection to an actual door. Refresh the approach description from current geometry after feature rebuilds; avoid stale copied endpoints. No broad feature/staircase redesign, ownership migration or generic reapply/provenance/cross-cell policy change.
Scope: lib/sources/garden_sources.py, lib/layers/ground_layer.py, decor_plan.py, decor_layer.py and their existing tests; narrowly scoped approach description in lib/builds/house_build.py and feature_build.py plus existing plan/journal metadata only as needed; rules/frontage-and-evidence.md and rules/handoff-layered-passes.md. Verification: synthetic partial-evidence residential strip, marked inference, per-house none/override, ineligible no-evidence property, mixed surfaces, gap surviving final joins, path joining an existing stoop, blocked-access report, diagonal/cell-edge and campus regression. Feature generates external steps plus cleared headroom; reload the landed journal/plan (air has no owner), then ground/decor preserve identical feature solids and reserved headroom including final joins. An updated feature approach changes its connection description without changing unrelated readiness policy. Missing legacy endpoint is explicit. Tests use disposable synthetic inputs, never world data. No live apply in tool task.
Separate world review after tool delivery: record best available street/aerial evidence and rebuild 53,-43 ground then decor, feature only if its own approach is faulty. Compare supplied reference camera for public/private separation, boundary openings, and connections to actual visible doors without duplicate/overwritten steps. Inspect evidence/inference reporting; owner judges coherent realism, not exact gate accuracy. Tool task can finish on synthetic checks; I-042 remains open for rebuild and owner verdict. Log the merged fix with issues.py fix and a check line for S-073.
Independent review: revised to reuse existing provenance, protect openings through all sources/final joins, bound residential inference, qualify blocked connections and separate world review; second fresh review clarified semantic clearance versus ownership of air. tasks.title: Sparse front boundaries in cell 53,-43 (Kitchener and Sirdar roads): walls, fences, hedges and gates
tasks.notes:
Owner review 2026-11-08 of 53,-43 (southampton-build): very little decor outside house fronts. Not measured yet. Related: #240 (shared frontage between ground and decor), snag S-073. Start by measuring decor per frontage against the aerial and street-run convention, then decide whether the cause is the decor layer or missing boundary evidence. Needs a live world to verify. Spun out of #243 (doors, closed).

DIAGNOSIS 2026-11-09 (read-only; decor report highfield_53_m43_decor-report.json + garden_sources.garden_barriers report).
Measure: 59 eligible fronts in the cell (Kitchener 31, Sirdar 28). 26 have no decor at all. 186 of 1,981 front-yard columns carry decor (~9%), all aerial-hedge fragments. Zero walls, fences or gates; zero furniture in the whole cell (furniture 0). Frontage `boundary` is empty on all 59. Sparse is true on both streets equally.
Aerial (reference/aerial/kitchener-z19 mosaic): fronts are not plain. Most have a low pale wall on the pavement line, side dividing walls or hedges, a paved drive or path gap, gravel/lawn with shrubs, some bins.
Where lost: (1) EVIDENCE, the main cause. A front boundary needs a `front` spec in site/gardens/<street>.json or an aerial hedge (hedge_share >= 0.6). kitchener_road.json has only rear/side vetoes, no `front`; sirdar_road.json does not exist. Aerial hedge fired on 12 of 59 front segments; low walls read pale, not green, so the detector cannot see them. (2) Aerial-hedge fronts never feed residential_frontage `boundary`/`opening` (role_spec only), so those hedges get no entrance gap from the opening logic (route columns are still reserved). (3) No source for private-yard furniture: only map furniture and reference/decor-furniture.json (no 53,-43 entry). (4) NOT the cause: layer drops inside fronts are 29 columns (22 against build, 5 above lidar, 2 blocked); route+clearance take 5-11 columns of 14-58 per yard.
Proposed fix: (a) world data, no code: add `front` (low wall, height 1) and `side_front` to kitchener_road.json and a new sirdar_road.json, citing a registered aerial evidence id; per-house `front: none` where the aerial shows an open drive. (b) code, garden_sources.residential_frontage / garden_barriers: pass the resolved front spec (convention or aerial hedge) into the frontage so `boundary` and `opening` are set for aerial hedges too; widen the opening to the drive width where the route meets a paved strip. Tests in lib/sources/test_garden_sources.py: aerial-hedge front gets an opening; convention front wall leaves the route open. (c) owner decision first: whether to add a front-yard furniture convention (bins beside the opening, planters), labelled inference.
Verify: per-front table before/after (decor columns in extent, boundary length, opening present), decor dry run on 53,-43, then an in-world look along both roads.

OWNER DECISION 2026-11-09: a front yard here should have walls, hedges, fences, bushes, ideally flowers, sheds, garages, ponds and gates. Every element still needs aerial or map evidence per property; nothing is scattered by default. Owning layer for each element: walls, fences, hedges, gates = decor (this task: front/side_front conventions, aerial hedge -> boundary and opening, gate block in the opening; gates are not built today, the opening is left as air). Bushes = trees (bush_voxels for small crowns; check whether front-yard shrubs show in the canopy mask or are lost). Flowers = ground foliage (foliage.py flower list; check whether guessed lawn in private frontage gets any). Sheds and garages = outbuildings: cell_features.py leaves them 'to their house plot' and coverage.py lists OUTBUILDINGS, but nothing appears to build them; this is a gap of its own. Ponds = only mapped natural=water polygons become water_body features; garden ponds from the aerial have no source. Split 2026-11-09 (owner agreed): this task keeps walls, fences, hedges and gates. Sheds and garages moved to #251; bushes, flowers and garden ponds moved to #252. RE-SCOPED 2026-11-10 (docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md): part (a) of the diagnosis, boundary evidence per street, overlaps #255 (district vibe profile); the aerial-hedge opening gap overlaps #240's open item; street furniture is now #260. Blocked by #255. What remains here: the live measurement and the in-world verification against the aerial.

tasks.title: site_lock.run crashes on macOS with PermissionError in its process-group cleanup and leaves the lock held (redo_layer.py)
tasks.notes: Seen 2026-11-09 on every `scripts/redo_layer.py --apply` run after the layers had applied and verified (southampton-build, macOS): traceback ends at lib/site/site_lock.py run(), `os.killpg(process.pid, 0)` in the post-exit grace loop, `PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted`. Only ProcessLookupError is caught, so on macOS (killpg on a group whose leader has exited can give EPERM, not ESRCH) the finally block aborts before the SIGKILL and `release(owner)`. Effects: the lock stays held by the redo-layer-<pid> owner (a later redo on another cell refuses with 'Held by redo-layer-N'), and the command exits 1 although the work succeeded. Workaround: `site_lock.py --world W release redo-layer-<pid>`. Also note `site_lock.py run ... -- redo_layer.py` cannot wrap redo_layer because it claims the lock itself ('Held by claude'). Fix: treat PermissionError like ProcessLookupError in both killpg calls, always reach release(owner) (nest in try/finally), and add a unit test with a mocked killpg raising PermissionError. Consider making redo_layer honour an existing SITE_OWNER instead of claiming a second lock.

tasks.title: Trial: rule-built typology buildings versus per-building specs (owner picks terrace, estate and shop parade)
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT: the owner names the world and three study streets, and says whether they may be rebuilt. Plan: docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md sections 2 and 6. Today houses use scripts/house_build.py (already a rule-based footprint builder with a small spec) and non-house buildings use a full hand-written spec in site/builds/<name>.json built by feature_build.py. Question: how much of a real district can rules cover well, using footprint, lidar height, OSM tags (building, building:levels, roof:shape) and a small per-district choice of palette and roof form. This is a spike. The prototype generates minimal specs for the existing builders (house_build and feature_build); it does not add a third builder. Baseline is house_build with a minimal spec versus a full feature_build spec for the same buildings. Study streets: a terrace, a semi-detached or detached estate street, a shop parade. Build about 20 buildings per street with the prototype and compare with the current path, noting minutes and session tokens per building (method stated) and what the player sees from the street. Pitched roofs use pitched_roof_states as it is today. Deliver findings in docs/plans/typology-buildings.md: which building classes the rules cover, what still needs a designer, cost per building under each path, and a recommendation, including whether roof and facade detail (I-006) and glazing become class recipes. File implementation tasks from the findings, not before. Scratch effects and snags go to the named world's repo. Check: findings file has a Cost heading and table rows; the owner's in-game verdict on whether the rule-built streets read as the real ones is recorded in it.

tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT: the owner names the world, an industrial estate or retail park and a high street, and says whether they may be rebuilt. Plan: docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md section 6. Using the #253 land-use classes, try per-class defaults by hand and with a throwaway prototype where cheap, reusing lib/layers/outbuildings.py for sheds and feature_build.py for larger massing: yard and car-park surfaces, fence and gate lines, loading bays, simple shed and warehouse massing with lidar height, shop frontages and awnings, forecourts, signage as plain colour blocks. Scratch effects and snags go to the named world's repo. Check: findings file has a Cost heading and recommended-table rows; the owner's in-game verdict is recorded in it.

tasks.title: Street furniture: labelled lamp and bench inference where the map has no points (I-008)
tasks.notes: Plan: docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md section 4. I-008: the vector-map cache for 48,-44 held no point features on 2026-10-27, so benches, bins, bike racks, lamp posts and bollards had no source. lib/sources/street_furniture.py already defines the kinds, recipes and extract presets. A candidate cause is #237 (the furniture preset failed under GDAL's default schema, world provider patch uncommitted); that is blocked on the owner and is not part of this task. Deliver the inference only: labelled street lamps along roads at a spacing set by OSM highway class (residential, tertiary and above, footway), benches at a low density on paths in park and leisure land (#253 classes), kept off door routes, entrance openings and carriageways, never reported as observed; a mapped point or designer trace wins. Spacing comes from the district profile (#255) when present, else a default per highway class. Whether OSM lit tags are available is unverified: use them when present, state when absent. This direction (2026-11-10) supersedes #244's 'nothing scattered by default' for street furniture only. Blocked by #254 because both change decor_plan and decor_layer. Files: lib/sources/street_furniture.py, lib/layers/decor_plan.py, decor_layer.py and their tests. Check: unit tests on synthetic road strips (spacing per highway class, door-route clearance, labelled inference, mapped point wins) via python3 scripts/run_tests.py --only <stem>; a dry-run decor report for one built cell shows furniture counts by provenance; no live apply. World review (separate, owner): rebuild decor in one cell and judge street feel.

tasks.title: House interior air must win over older ground paving (I-040 S-075): measure, then fix
tasks.notes: I-040 snag S-075: after rebuilding houses_sirdar_road_w177806445 (2026-11-09), cells inside the footprint at x6866-6872, z-5497..-5489 still hold gray_concrete at y35, one block above the house floor (b=34), because the house plan's interior air at b+1 is dropped by the earlier-owner clash filter where an older ground build owns paving. Doors are now kept; interior cells are not. Not measured across other plans. Step 1 (read-only): list, for every landed house plan, the interior columns where an older ground build still owns a block at floor+1, with counts per plan; reuse scripts/door_audit.py's approach or its live reads. Step 2: change the clash handling so house interior air at floor+1 cancels older ground paving inside the footprint (journal CANCEL and air-cancels rules preserved; ownership of other cells unchanged), with a synthetic test, and file or note the rebuild list for the world repo. Related: #234 (cross-cell edge policy, blocked on the owner) and #249 (door audit). Files: lib/site/site_kit.py or the journal clash filter (locate first), tests. Check: unit test on a synthetic ground-then-house plan showing interior air wins and neighbours do not change, via python3 scripts/run_tests.py --only <stem>; step 1's per-plan count table is in the task notes. No live apply in this task; rebuilds are world work.

tasks.title: Provider-neutral lidar: ghost, query, extremes and readiness resolve by type; a world's own lidar row beats the system row; documented provider contract
tasks.notes: Owner direction 2026-11-10: other people using the toolkit install their own providers; tool code asks for a reference type, never a vendor (#28 covered only the lidar world and tiles modules). Plan: docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md. Evidence (checked in code): (1) shims/lidar_ghost.py, lidar_query.py and lidar_extremes.py call load_provider('ukdefra-lidar', ...) with a literal id; callers are lib/layers/ground_layer.py:119, lib/journal/cell_preparation.py:57, scripts/cell_registry.py:132 and 149, scripts/cell_marker.py:470 and 494. (2) load_place_sources (lib/sources/cell_sources.py ~99-110) lists system rows before world rows and lidar_provider_row returns the first lidar match, so a locally installed lidar row never beats the system one, for world and tiles too. (3) lib/journal/readiness_evidence.py lidar_status (~63-85) uses pick_uri, TILE_MB, tiles_for and client.cache/catalogue/<E>E-<N>N.json and client.tiles, a provider-specific interface that cell preparation depends on. (4) lib/sources/test_lidar_provider.py mocks load_lidar_module, so it checks row choice only. (5) ghost planning catches LookupError as 'no lidar for cell', so a no-provider LookupError would be swallowed. Reviewer-checked: lidar_ghost is vendor-neutral apart from a 4-line default_heights, and ghost_owners_for needs no lidar; lidar_query and lidar_extremes hard-import defra_lidar, DEFRA_CRS and --bbox-osgb; no core code imports them, but .agents/skills/new-world-build/SKILL.md:90 names lidar_extremes. Unverified: whether a provider outside England can meet the readiness tile interface as it stands. Deliver: (a) world-over-system precedence for the lidar catalogue row, with a test; (b) lidar_ghost as shared code that samples through lidar_provider (not a catalogue role), with default_heights moved into the provider; (c) query and extremes as catalogue modules roles resolved by type, copying the shims/lidar_world.py pattern; (d) readiness_evidence.lidar_status reads missing tiles and tile identity through a provider-neutral method on the tile client; (e) a typed no-provider error instead of LookupError; (f) extend the lidar contract already in reference/TYPES.txt (and fix its stale scripts/ path) with entry points, model names DTM and DSM, missing(), sample(), the mc_heights keys, crs and the tile and cost methods, and update the seams table in docs/provider-name-audit.md. Out of scope: writing a real second provider; a fallback height source where no lidar exists. Files: shims/lidar_ghost.py, lidar_query.py, lidar_extremes.py, _provider_shim.py; lib/sources/lidar_provider.py, cell_sources.py, config/system-providers.json; lib/layers/ground_layer.py; lib/journal/cell_preparation.py, readiness_evidence.py; scripts/cell_registry.py, cell_marker.py; reference/TYPES.txt; docs/provider-name-audit.md; tests. Check: a new test with a synthetic second lidar provider in a temp world, with the system row still present, run in a fresh process (scripts/run_tests.py is one process and the shims overwrite sys.modules): the shims, the registry and readiness pick it up; a static assertion that no catalogue id appears in shims/lidar_*.py; python3 scripts/check_provider_names.py still passes. Trials #256-#259 outside the first world's country depend on this being done or on the trial naming its own height source.
